Those are both really good points. The first was an intentional design decision. I wanted there to be some resentment of the nobility. I wanted the nobles to have to force everyone to do things they didn't like. Give the nobles more money and more problems. I wasn't as involved as I was hoping to be in that development, so I feel that it fell a bit flat. I don't think I would want to put that negative responsibility on players next time. It didn't really live up to my hopes.

The second point was also a design choice. Adjudicating custom items is very fun, and a good outlet for collaborative creativity, but this crafting system was designed specifically to not have to do that. It takes a lot of time making sure you produce a power balanced item that does what the player hopes. I really like doing that, but in season 2, it felt too arbitrary as to what people got. For better or for worse, the loudest and most aggressive players ended up with with the most custom loot. The squeaky wheel gets the grease. This year, the goal was to make a system that pretty much could run itself. And I think it did that well. But I also know we can do better.

**Oath of Arachne**
The Oath of Arachne is a curious and often unheard-of order of paladins, who model their virtues after those of the humble spider. To those familiar with the order, they are known as spider-knights, snare-soldiers, or ironclad crawlers. Binding oneself to the Oath of Arachne is often a difficult task, as few established orders exist, and tend to be more localized than many others. The Oath of Arachne is also home to all kinds, including those with not-so-pure intentions. Undertakers of this oath are often followers of Lolth, Anansi, or another local spider-related deity, such as the New Orleans demigod Web. 

**Tennants of Arachne**
The tenants of the Oath of Arachne tend to vary from order to order, especially between orders following different deities. But regardless of how they are changed, the tenants tend to follow this basic form.
`Know Your Enemy`
In order to best solve a problem, you must first understand that problem. The easiest solution is often not the best.
`Kill With Purpose`
Just as spiders kill to feed themselves or their young, a foe should not be killed for no reason. An enemy's body should be honored and made use of. 
`Be Patient, be Prepared`
Do not blindly seek out your enemy, lest you end up making more in their place. By your words and deeds you will make yourself known and enemies will seek you out. Be ready, just as a spider spins its web.
`Continue the Cycle`
Just as life and death pass fluidly into one another, so should your tenets pass on to the next generation. Your actions must create lasting change, not just a momentary reprieve.
